captured.title: How households took over the bank loan book
captured.description: In June 2026 individuals owed ₹47 of every ₹100 Indian banks had lent and private companies ₹27, against ₹31 and ₹40 in March 2015. Individuals' loan accounts tripled while the average loan, after prices, did not grow. A data story from the Reserve Bank's Basic Statistical Returns.
headers: How households took over the bank loan book
Bank loans to companies doubled on paper, only rose a quarter in real terms
Individuals’ loan accounts tripled from 2015 to 2026
Personal loans went from ₹16.5 to ₹30.9 of every ₹100 banks lent, 2015 to 2026
Women’s loan accounts peaked in June 2024 and have fallen since
In short
Individuals owe ₹47 of every ₹100 banks have lent, private companies ₹27
Individuals’ loan accounts tripled, and the average loan is about 5% smaller after prices
Women hold 30 of every 100 accounts of individuals and ₹24.5 of every ₹100

captured.title: The ₹2 lakh line
captured.description: Nearly two in every three bank loans in India have a limit of ₹2 lakh or less. They hold ₹6 of every ₹100 banks have lent, carry the highest interest rates in the banks’ books, and there are about 4 crore fewer of them at banks than at the end of 2024. A data story from the Reserve Bank’s own figures.
headers: The ₹2 lakh line
Villages lost loans filed as farm credit, while big cities lost durable-loan accounts
Loans to women fell, most steeply in the east
Ten districts hold ₹42 of every ₹100
In short
Small loans have doubled since 2017
The smallest loans carry the highest rates in the banks’ books
Small loans fell by about 4 crore between 2024 and 2026
The counts hold, but they count accounts rather than people, include one merger and place loans where they are booked

captured.description: Of the 697 goods in India’s wholesale price index, 33 cost less in 2025-26 than in 2011-12 and 103 cost at least twice as much. Consumer prices rose 77% between 2013 and 2025, wholesale prices 40%
623 of 697 goods cost fewer days’ wages at wholesale than in 2014-15
Grown goods cost about 17 times what they did in 1982-83; factory goods about 8 times
In short
The figures hold; the index prices goods at the factory gate, with no services and no allowance for a better TV

As UPI payments grew 19.4x, debit-card payments fell 75.7%

₹500 notes are 85.5% of the value of banknotes in March 2026, up from 47.8% in March 2016

captured.title: Money in, money out
captured.description: Indians abroad sent home $135.4 billion in 2024-25, and kept $165.7 billion in Indian banks. Indians at home sent $29.6 billion abroad. Built from the data published on the Reserve Bank’s DBIE.
headers: Money in,money out
In 2024-25, Indians abroad sent home $135.4 bn, and Indians at home sent $29.6 bn abroad
Which brought India more foreign money in 2023-24: foreign companies investing, or Indians abroad sending money home?
Money sent home rose from $0.2 bn in 1973-74 to $2.7 bn in 1980-81, and to $135.4 bn by 2024-25
Over 19 years, money sent home moved 11.6% in a typical year and FDI 34.8%; in the pandemic year 2020-21 it dipped 3.6%
In 2023-24 the US sent 27.7% of India’s remittances and the UAE 19.2%; in 2016-17 the UAE led, with 26.9%
It landed first in Maharashtra (20.5%) and Kerala (19.7%); five states received 66.4%
Indians abroad kept $165.7 bn in Indian bank deposits at the end of March 2026, 1.22x a year’s money sent home
Twice the RBI opened a window for dollar deposits: FCNR(B) deposits rose $25.8 bn after September 2013, and the 2026 window drew $65.40 bn in under eleven weeks
One resident may send $250,000 abroad a year; the limit began at $25,000 on 04-02-2004 and was cut once, to $75,000 on 14-08-2013
Indians sent $29.6 bn abroad under the LRS in 2024-25, 6.4x 2015-16; travel was $17.0 bn of it, 57.4%
Money sent for study abroad peaked at $5.2 bn in 2021-22 and was $2.9 bn in 2024-25
In the month tax collected at source began, and in the month it rose, money sent abroad fell: 43.1% in October 2020, 37.7% in October 2023
For every $100 that came into India from Indians abroad in 2024-25, $22 went out of India under the LRS
$135.4 bn in; $165.7 bn kept; $29.6 bn out
